speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where the wrist pain is located and describe what the skin lesions look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of migratory joint pain, recent camping in Minnesota, and fever strongly suggests Lyme disease. Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions, specifically if they have a target-like or bull's-eye pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" you described are highly specific and point away from Lyme disease toward a different diagnosis. I need to rule out secondary syphilis or other systemic infections, so I will order some specific blood work. REQUEST TEST: RPR, HIV, CBC, ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RPR: Not ordered/pending; HIV: Negative; CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; ESR: Not ordered/pending

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of migratory arthritis, fever, and painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the extremities is classic for disseminated gonococcal infection. I need to confirm this with specific cultures. REQUEST TEST: Gonorrhea NAAT, Blood Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Gonorrhea NAAT: Positive; Blood Culture: Pending

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Gonorrhea NAAT confirms the diagnosis of disseminated gonococcal infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
